name: ARC
ability_definition: The ability to generate or use different sets of rules for combining or grouping things in different ways.

task_realism.reasoning: Workplace Category Flexibility looks like re-sorting inventory by different attributes, reclassifying cases or documents under new schemes, or regrouping data for different analyses. ARC tasks are abstract colored-grid transformations. Some tasks do require grouping cells or objects by color, shape, or position under a newly induced rule, which is a real but distant echo of that activity. Most tasks are about spatial transformation rather than flexible grouping.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Each task is a fresh few-shot induction problem with no feedback-driven rule switching. The system never regroups the same items under a new rule and is never penalized for clinging to an old rule, which is exactly what real work and WCST-style probes demand. Setting: offline, no tools, a few attempts, exact-match grading. That differs from workplace conditions, where people iterate, get feedback, have domain context, and face ambiguous criteria.

construct_coverage.reasoning: ARC does test generating a novel rule from sparse examples, which is one component of the ability. It omits producing multiple alternative groupings of the same set, switching rules when conditions change, and resisting perseveration. It also mixes in many unrelated skills: spatial reasoning, counting, symmetry, and object persistence. Overall it is a narrow and contaminated slice, consistent with the selection step's 4/10 coverage judgment.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are small integer-colored grids and outputs are exact grids, a highly artificial toy format. Real artifacts for this ability are item lists, spreadsheets, taxonomies, case files, and categorization schemes described in language. None of these resemble ARC's inputs or outputs.

transferability_reasoning: ARC captures the rule-induction part of Category Flexibility but not its core features: regrouping the same items under several rules and switching rules on feedback without perseverating. Its abstract grid format and one-shot evaluation are far from workplace categorization tasks. ARC performance should be read as a weak, loose proxy for this ability rather than evidence of real workplace capability.

2020.model_or_system: Icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind): brute-force search over a hand-written library of 142 grid functions (a domain-specific language)
2020.metric: percent of tasks solved (top-3 accuracy) on the 100-task hidden private test set
2020.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce (typical adults doing novel visual rule-induction puzzles)

2022.model_or_system: icecuber (winner of the 2020 ARC competition on Kaggle, a program-synthesis/DSL search solver)
2022.metric: percent of hidden private-test tasks solved (exact-match output, up to 3 attempts per task in the 2020 Kaggle protocol)
2022.human_reference: General adult population, typical educated workers doing novel rule-induction and regrouping tasks without specialist training
